what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Suriname in all host countries: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 152 Surinamese asylum seekers, and the United States hosted 32.2% of them.
After the United States, the largest hosts are Brazil, Belgium and France.

why.text: The fact pack records no armed conflict and no dated events for Suriname, so it does not say why people left.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2020 and 2022 to 2025.

when.text: UNHCR's series starts in 2000 at 48 asylum seekers, and the figure fell to a low in 2011.
The figure was at its highest, 251, at the end of 2024.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took.
These are year-end totals summed over every host country that reported to UNHCR.
